PMID:39517369.topic: Oral nutritional supplementation after hip fracture
PMID:39517369.setting: 29 hospitals (24 Australian, 5 New Zealand) taking part in the ANZ Hip Fracture Registry Nutrition Sprint Audit
PMID:39517369.standard: ESPEN guideline and ANZ Hip Fracture Clinical Care Standard: all older adults with hip fracture should be offered oral nutritional supplements regardless of nutritional status

cycle1.result: ONS provided or prescribed for 182/385 (47.3%) of older adults having hip fracture surgery. ONS was more likely if malnourished on formal testing (OR 11.92; 95% CI 6.57, 21.69).

PMID:39517369.other_findings: ONS was also more likely with no preoperative medical assessment (OR 2.26), cognitive impairment (OR 1.83) and severe frailty or terminal illness (OR 3.17); New Zealand patients were less likely to receive ONS (OR 0.45). 30.9% of patients were diagnosed as malnourished.

PMID:38024083.setting: Two centres of one trauma and orthopaedic service (Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust / North Manchester General Hospital), knee arthroscopy day cases
PMID:38024083.standard: Correct ICD-10 and OPCS-4 coding of arthroscopic knee procedures from the operation note; proforma based on Royal College guidance for operation notes

cycle1.result: 17/34 (50%) cases coded incorrectly; tariff value £85,026 as coded versus £114,351 after correction, a loss of £29,325.

PMID:38024083.intervention: New coding-friendly knee arthroscopy operation note proforma with tick boxes, developed with coding staff and agreed at a consensus meeting, disseminated by email, notice boards and governance meetings.

cycle2.result: 2/37 (5%) cases coded incorrectly; £86,886 as coded versus £89,540 after correction, a loss of £2654.

PMID:38024083.other_findings: Most coding errors came from vague documentation of preoperative diagnoses and additional procedures (e.g. extra meniscectomy or cartilage debridement). Uptake of the proforma was slow and some cases were excluded for incorrect use of the form.

PMID:39130507.setting: Elective orthopaedic theatre lists (excluding spine and trauma), William Harvey Hospital, Ashford
PMID:39130507.standard: No existing standard; locally defined datapoints (surgical team, anaesthesia type, side, prosthesis/equipment, fluoroscopy, acronyms, extra patient information), later adopted as the 'William Harvey theatre list standard'

cycle1.result: 115 lists, 326 cases. Consultant in charge recorded in 85%; lead anaesthetist missing in 4.3%; 98% listed as GA (spinal 0.3%); 76.8% had no prosthesis/equipment detail; fluoroscopy requirement stated in 11% of cases needing it; acronyms used in 28%; extra patient information in 6%.

PMID:39130507.intervention: Proforma of essential information for waiting list coordinators, minor IT changes to the theatre list input form, and education of waiting list coordinators and trainees.

cycle2.result: 100 lists, 255 cases. Consultant in charge recorded in 100%; 80% listed as GA (14.5% spinal per abstract; 37 regional); no prosthesis/equipment detail fell to 43% (abstract: prosthesis/equipment mentioned 34% vs 23%); fluoroscopy stated in 25% of cases needing it; acronyms 6%; extra patient information 49.8%.

PMID:39130507.other_findings: Lead anaesthetist was missing in 16% of lists at re-audit (worse than 4.3%), and only 5.3% of hip arthroplasty cases stated cement requirement in both rounds. A staff questionnaire (38/40 completed) informed the datapoints.

PMID:26981239.topic: Ankle fracture management in older adults
PMID:26981239.setting: Bristol Royal Infirmary, patients aged 50 to 80 admitted with ankle fractures
PMID:26981239.standard: No best-practice standard stated for management; DEXA scanning in patients over 65 compared with NICE (2011) osteoporosis recommendations

cycle1.result: 42 (84%) operative and 8 (16%) non-operative. Malunion (63%) and failed fixation (25%) more common after non-operative care. Formal bone protection strategy in 3 patients (6%); only 3 patients (14%) aged over 65 had a DEXA scan.

PMID:26981239.other_findings: Malunion and failed fixation were significantly higher after surgery without consultant supervision (p = 0.043). Recommendations were DEXA for all over 65s and consultant supervision for bi- and trimalleolar fixation; re-audit was outside the project scope.

PMID:42333334.setting: District general hospital emergency department and associated nurse-led Minor Injury Unit, Mid and South Essex NHS Trust (Basildon)
PMID:42333334.standard: NICE NG38: non-rigid immobilisation (removable splint or bandage) and discharge without routine follow-up for distal radius torus fractures; target 100%

cycle1.result: Compliance 97/174 (56%) at DGH and 0/48 (0%) at MIU, combined 97/222 (44%). Rigid immobilisation 77/174 (44%) DGH and 48/48 (100%) MIU. Fracture clinic follow-up 128/222 (58%).

PMID:42333334.intervention: Educational posters in ED and MIU, NG38 emailed to all clinical staff, teaching sessions (two at DGH, one at MIU) and reinforcement at governance meetings (October 2023 to February 2024).

cycle2.result: Compliance 131/164 (80%) at DGH (p < 0.001) and 29/94 (31%) at MIU (p < 0.001), combined 160/258 (62%). Fracture clinic follow-up 98/258 (38%) (p < 0.001).

PMID:42333334.other_findings: Rigid immobilisation persisted in 33/164 (20%) at DGH and 65/94 (69%) at MIU; splint stock at the MIU may have contributed. No balancing measures were collected.

PMID:41573452.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (major trauma centre)
PMID:41573452.standard: Royal College of Physicians Health Informatics Unit 2019 discharge summary content standards

cycle1.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 15.6% (5/32); new medication indication documented 9.4% (3/32); patient advice fully detailed 21.2% (7/33); inpatient management fully detailed 30.3% (10/33).

PMID:41573452.intervention: Educational poster with a checklist of RCP components, interactive teaching sessions, a discharge summary self-assessment checklist, reminders with one-to-one feedback for junior doctors and a team campaign (August to September 2025).

cycle2.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 90.0% (18/20) (p < 0.0001); new medication indication 50.0% (9/18) (p = 0.004); patient advice fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.0002); inpatient management fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.001).

PMID:41573452.other_findings: Any safety-net advice fell from 96.9% (32/33) to 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.02), though when present it was more often excellent. Seven-day readmission was 6.1% vs 4.8%, with no change.

PMID:31353806.setting: Single-centre MRI service (QLD X-ray, QEII Hospital, Brisbane), 3T scanner

cycle1.result: 31 patients (32 knees). DIXON images judged comparable replacements for sagittal PD and PD fat-saturated sequences with no loss of diagnostic confidence; reviewer 1 mean image quality 1.56 and fat suppression 1.19; scan time saving just over 10% (about 1 minute per patient).

PMID:31353806.other_findings: Patient motion affected 5 series (15.6%) and a minor chemical shift artefact was seen at the femoral cartilage, neither affecting diagnosis.

PMID:39483602.topic: Hip fracture operation choice per NICE guidance
PMID:39483602.setting: Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge (major trauma centre), patients over 65 having hip fracture surgery
PMID:39483602.standard: NICE CG124 Section 1.6 (choice of arthroplasty, THR for eligible displaced intracapsular fractures, extramedullary implants for A1/A2 trochanteric fractures, intramedullary nail for subtrochanteric fractures)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 76.04% (1244/1636). THR documented as considered in 43.6% (193/443) of eligible patients; 56.43% of THR-indicated patients had no documented consideration (65.41% in 2020).

PMID:39483602.intervention: A 'smart phrase' NICE THR-eligibility checklist added to the electronic (Epic) neck of femur clerking proforma in June 2021.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 87.43% (459/525) (z = 5.556, p < 0.01). THR considered in 57.89% (77/133); 42.11% of THR-indicated patients lacked documented consideration (z = 2.904, p < 0.01).

PMID:39483602.other_findings: The proportion of patients actually receiving THR did not increase, and use of the smart phrase declined over time without a drop in compliance. NICE CG124 changed in January 2023, making the smart phrase outdated.

PMID:41773159.setting: Orthopaedic department, Prince Osman Digna Referral Hospital, Port Sudan (tertiary referral centre), handwritten notes
PMID:41773159.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice: 18 core operation note criteria

cycle1.dates: not reported (audit ran May 2024 to May 2025)
cycle1.result: Anticipated blood loss, antibiotic prophylaxis and DVT prophylaxis each 0/50 (0%); operative findings 17/50 (34%); tissue removed/altered 16/50 (32%); surgical approach 20/50 (40%); surgeon name 49/50 (98%).

PMID:41773159.intervention: Presentation of findings at a governance meeting, distribution and discussion of RCS operation note standards, and senior-led feedback and reinforcement in theatre.

cycle2.result: Anticipated blood loss 10/35 (28.6%); antibiotic prophylaxis 7/35 (20%); DVT prophylaxis 5/35 (14.3%); operative findings 26/35 (74.3%); tissue altered 25/35 (71.4%); surgical approach 28/35 (80%); surgeon name 35/35 (100%).

PMID:41773159.other_findings: Elective/emergency status stayed poor at 11/35 (31.4%) and surgeon signature was 30/35 (85.7%). The authors recommend a mandatory operation note template.

PMID:41664757.setting: District general hospital, patients aged 60 or over with neck of femur fracture who had pre-operative TTE
PMID:41664757.standard: Local trust guideline: no surgical delay awaiting echo; TTE only for listed indications; all TTE reports acknowledged by the anaesthetist; target 100%

cycle1.result: No surgical delay 12/12 (100%); appropriate requests 4/12 (33.3%); reports acknowledged by anaesthetist 10/12 (83.3%).

PMID:41664757.intervention: Teaching sessions, posters of request criteria, dissemination of audit findings, reminders at safety meetings and printed prompt cards.

cycle2.result: No surgical delay 17/17 (100%); appropriate requests 16/17 (94.1%); reports acknowledged 12/17 (70.6%).

PMID:41664757.other_findings: Acknowledgement of echo reports fell. TTE findings changed anaesthetic management in 4/17 (23.5%), mainly invasive arterial monitoring.

PMID:34900463.setting: Nine NHS hospitals across six university health boards in Wales, trainee collaborative (WORC) prospective snapshot audit
PMID:34900463.standard: BOAST guideline on management of ankle fractures (documentation, imaging including CT for posterior malleolus, weight-bearing X-rays, early weight-bearing)

cycle1.result: Documentation: mechanism 94.4%, skin 71.3%, neurovascular status 80.1%, comorbidities 81%, alcohol 34.3%, smoking 41.7%. Mortice view 75.9%. CT for posterior malleolus fracture 15/31 (48.38%) operative and 0/9 non-operative. Weight-bearing X-ray in non-operative group 22/106 (20.8%). Early weight-bearing 63/106 (59.43%) non-operative and 11/110 (10%) operative.

PMID:34900463.other_findings: Reason for delayed weight-bearing after surgery was documented in only 16/99 (16.16%). Education, an infographic and a re-audit were planned.

PMID:39171035.topic: Ottawa ankle and knee rules compliance
PMID:39171035.setting: Emergency department and urgent treatment centre, Lincoln County Hospital (district general hospital)
PMID:39171035.standard: Ottawa Ankle and Knee Rules (incorporated in NICE guidance) for requesting X-rays

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 59.5%; knee X-rays 74.6% (n=182); ankle X-rays 33.1% (n=46). Positivity 18.0% knee and 32.0% ankle.

PMID:39171035.intervention: Educational session, leaflets, posters in ED and UTC and emails to clinicians (August 2023).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 85% (221/260); knee X-rays 89.9% (152); ankle X-rays 75.8% (69). Positivity 18.9% knee and 44.0% ankle.

PMID:39171035.other_findings: Compliance was much lower for patients under 55 (22.5% in cycle 1, 69.9% in cycle 2). Compliance was judged from radiology requests only.

PMID:30463777.setting: Regional referral hospitals in Cameroon (Delphi panel of surgeons and interviews at three facilities)

cycle1.result: Panel of 7 surgeons: 23 of 40 audit filter variables met consensus and 21 had median score of 4 or more (e.g. vitals, breathing assessment and two large-bore IVs within 15 min; IV antimicrobials within 1 h for open fractures). 16 providers interviewed.

PMID:30463777.other_findings: Barriers were limited staff and materials and patients' inability to pay; regular trauma training and staff buy-in were seen as promoters.

PMID:3198269.topic: Accuracy of emergency department fracture clinic referrals
PMID:3198269.setting: Acute orthopaedic (fracture) clinic receiving Accident and Emergency referrals, Yorkshire Regional Health Authority

cycle1.result: 17.2% had an incorrect diagnosis and 12% had been incorrectly treated; 49.4% of plaster splints were removed and 25.4% substantially altered; 6% admitted from clinic.

PMID:3198269.other_findings: Authors argue for audit and direct feedback to A&E staff to improve care and use of resources.
